profile_name: Nelson Mandela Bay Metropolitan Municipality (Port Elizabeth / Uitenhage / Despatch)
_doc:
SCANNED-IMAGE LEDGER BILL. 11 of the 12 calibration PDFs carry NO text layer at all (1 image per page, 0 text chars); read_pdf(ocr='auto') OCRs them via Tesseract at 300dpi and _ocr_words_to_text rebuilds columns from word boxes, so [ \t]{2,} column gaps work but individual DIGITS are unreliable (0/9, 7/2, 8/6, 8/5, 7/f, 3/#). Every row from those pages is force-flagged 'OCR - verify figures against the PDF'. That flag is correct: do not suppress it.

LAYOUT (OCR shape, 11 files): a running account LEDGER, not a metered bill.
  header       NELSON MANDELA BAY MUNICIPALITY | TAX INVOICE <MMDD NNNNNN>
               VAT No 4490193473 / DEPOSIT <amt> / Statement Date <YYYYMMDD>
               Account Number <12 digits> / UniPay Number 9100 x <account> x
               '<HOLDER> REG. NO 1999/018572/07' = account holder (site name)
  ledger       BROUGHT FORWARD <amt>
               dd/mm  DR#### DEBIT ADJUSTMENT   <amt>       <- ELECTRICITY ex VAT
                      CONSUMPTION   ELEC   <YYYY/MM>        <- consumption month
               dd/mm  DR#### DEBIT ADJUSTMENT   <amt>       <- ELECTRICITY VAT
                      CONSUMPTION   ELEC   VAT
               dd/mm  UNMETERED FIRE SUPPL      <amt>       <- WATER ex VAT
                      VAT @ 15.0%  <vat>  <inc>             <- water VAT + inc VAT
               dd/mm  ...THANK YOU FOR YOUR PAYMENT <amt>CR / INTEREST / ROUNDING DISCOUNT
               <bare amount on its own line>                <- closing subtotal = TOTAL PAYABLE
               TOTAL PAYABLE R <amt> / THIS MONTH: R <amt> / PAYABLE BEFORE: yyyy-mm-dd

NO METER, NO READINGS, NO kWh, NO TARIFF, NO DEMAND are printed anywhere on this bill - it is a consolidated unmetered/bulk account billed as a monthly DEBIT ADJUSTMENT. All of those canonical columns are mapped '_none' deliberately. The electricity charge goes to other_r (NOT standard_r): there is no kWh, and standard_r would raise a false 0KWH+ENERGY exception.

RULE ZERO / RECONCILE IS CIRCULAR HERE. The bill prints the electricity charge exactly ONCE (the ex-VAT DEBIT ADJUSTMENT amount). total_ex_vat_r and other_r therefore both read that same figure and 'reconcile' trivially - that check proves nothing. The real, independent checks are:
  (a) elec VAT == 15% of elec ex VAT  (two separately printed numbers)
  (b) fire ex + fire VAT == fire inc VAT (three separately printed numbers)
  (c) the closing subtotal line == BROUGHT FORWARD +/- every ledger line.

12th FILE HAS A REAL TEXT LAYER (NMBM_[number removed]_[number removed].pdf, 2,980 chars, 0 images): a clerk-printed 'Consolidated Billing / STATEMENT FOR ACCOUNT' report (CBS06021.QRP) covering TWO months (last billed + current). Its meta is read by the fallback patterns below; the FIRST month block wins (first-match, no collect:sum), which is the completed/billed month carrying 'TAX INVOICE NO'. Its ledger amounts use SOUTH AFRICAN COMMA DECIMALS ('489 068,70'), which the app's _to_decimal strips as a thousands separator - 489068,70 would become [number removed].00, a 100x error. Every money pattern here therefore REQUIRES a period decimal ('\.\d{2}'), so that file yields correct meta and BLANK money rather than wrong money. The verbatim strings are captured into nmb_*_printed text fields so a human can read them. Fixing this properly needs a one-line locale change in _to_decimal, not a profile change.

WHY MONEY PATTERNS ARE STRICT: the thousands group is '(?:[ ,]?\d{3})*', i.e. exactly three digits per group and at most ONE separator. That is deliberate. OCR turns '97 388.37' into '07   388.37' and '77 527.35' into 'i?   527.35'; a looser pattern captures 7388.37 / 527.35 - plausible, wrong, and unflagged. With the strict pattern those fields MISS instead. A miss is visible in Diagnostics; a wrong number is not.

CALIBRATION LIMIT: all 12 files are ONE account ([number removed], Telkom SA Ltd consolidated). NMBM's per-site metered bills will print a meter/reading/kWh table this profile has no rules for; those will route here (the fingerprint is correct) but produce only the ledger fields. Add metered rules when such a bill appears.
DELIBERATELY NOT MAPPED — recon prev_balance and incoming_payment. Both are single printed figures with no on-bill cross-check, and OCR gets them wrong often enough to be untrustworthy: over the 12 calibration bills BROUGHT FORWARD came out 6 right / 2 wrong (576 930.00 for 526 930.00; 749 651.40 for 749 851.40) / 4 unreadable, and THANK YOU FOR YOUR PAYMENT 3 right / 2 wrong (472 733.15 for 772 733.15; 568 497.95 for 568 492.95) / 7 unreadable - and it only ever captures the FIRST of up to two payments in a month. Neither adds anything: BROUGHT FORWARD is by definition the previous statement's closing subtotal, which recon 'subtotal' reads correctly on 11 of 11 scans. Leaving them out is what keeps this profile's output correct-or-blank with no wrong numbers anywhere. Re-enable only with a digit-verified OCR pass. The regexes were:
  prev_balance     BROUGHT FORWARD[ \t]{2,}((?<![\d.])-?\d{1,3}(?:[ ,]?\d{3})*\.\d{2}(?:[ \t]*[Cc][Rr])?)
  incoming_payment THANK YOU FOR YOUR PAYMENT[ \t]{2,}((?<![\d.])\d{1,3}(?:[ ,]?\d{3})*\.\d{2})(?=[ \t]*[Cc]?[Rr])

APP-LEVEL FINDINGS (not fixable in a profile):
 1. _to_decimal() strips ',' as a thousands separator, so it cannot read South African comma-decimal money at all ('489 068,70' -> [number removed].00). NMBM's consolidated statement uses it.
 2. _recon_money() does s.replace('R','') BEFORE testing for a trailing 'CR', so any recon capture ending in upper-case 'CR' ('749 852.90CR') is silently blanked. Affects every profile that captures trailing-CR credits into a recon column.
 3. _exc_date() cannot parse 'YYYYMMDD', which is how this bill prints its statement date, so no date-based exceptions (DUE<BILL, BILL-FUTURE, BILL-OLD) can fire on NMB rows.
 4. Raising the OCR dpi does NOT fix these scans - it trades errors (400dpi repairs '07 388.37'->'97 388.37' but breaks '73 812.07'->'73 612.07'; 600dpi is worse). The amount column is printed on a pale-blue shaded band with JPEG colour fringing. Greyscale + autocontrast + unsharp + per-line --psm 7 recovers some ('49? 332.98' -> '492 332.98') but not all. The real fix is source-side: NMBM's own e-billing produces text PDFs (this pack contains one), so ask for those.
